findings.title: `:tmpdir` / `:slash_tmp` deny entries are not enforced by the pinned CLI — /tmp stays readable and writable, and the new .codex/.git protection silently disappears for any workspace placed under /tmp
findings.detail: Round-1 HIGH v2-profile-project-dot-codex-writable is genuinely fixed and I re-verified it independently: with the rendered profile from packages/teamlead/dist and a fixture project under ~/.flywheel/qa, `codex sandbox --permission-profile flywheel-lead-v2 --cd <project>` produced SOURCE_WRITE_OK, CODEX_DIR_DENIED, GIT_CONFIG_DENIED, GIT_HOOK_DENIED, CODEX_DIR_MOVE_DENIED, HOME_READ_DENIED (codex-cli 0.153.2), and runtime-parent.ts now pins the effective mcp_servers set. What remains is the placement sensitivity behind the Lead's earlier exit-41 run. The same probe with the identical profile but the fixture under /private/tmp returns CODEX_DIR_WRITABLE, GIT_CONFIG_WRITABLE, GIT_HOOK_WRITABLE, CODEX_DIR_MOVABLE — i.e. everything the fix is meant to protect is writable again — and in BOTH placements the shell reports TMP_READABLE and TMP_WRITABLE for /private/tmp even though the profile sets `":tmpdir": "deny"` and `":slash_tmp": "deny"` (lines 81-82). So (a) those two deny entries buy nothing on the pinned CLI, and the model shell can read and write /tmp — where this repo's own tooling parks isolated CODEX_HOME copies (quota-probe runbook), ship reports, QA evidence and the parent's app-server socket dir (/tmp/fw-tui-*, capability-app-server.ts:35); and (b) the .codex/.git guarantee holds only because production places the workspace under $HOME. Mitigating: I could not escalate /tmp reachability into the app-server socket — a unix connect from inside the sandbox to a /tmp socket failed fast (CONNECT_DENIED) while the same nc connect outside the sandbox connected, so the unix_sockets allowlist does hold. Failure scenario: a Lead workspace, deployment checkout or TMPDIR relocated under /tmp (or a future QA slot fixture) silently loses .codex/.git protection with no assertion firing. Suggested fix: make leadModelWritableRoot()/profileConfig() reject a project or workspace root under /tmp or $TMPDIR (fail closed), since the design doc already concedes the host proof covers only the tested non-temp shape.

findings.title: The new filesystem[":workspace_roots"] table is compared byte-for-byte against real config/read output, but this round's host proofs never exercised config/read
findings.detail: assertLeadPermissionProfile() (permission-profile.ts:160-182) deep-equals the whole `permissions` table from the app-server's `config/read` result against `profileConfig(spec)`, and comparablePermissions() only normalizes a hand-listed set of null-valued fields observed on Codex 0.153.2. This round changed the shape of that table (`:workspace_roots` went from `{".": "write"}` to `{".codex": "read", ".git": "read"}`), but the two host proofs recorded in design-correction.md exercise `codex sandbox` (metadata canary) and `codex mcp list` / a native getxattr helper — neither goes through config/read. The unit coverage is a fixture that feeds back `parse(render(...))` plus the parent's own MCP argv (default-parent-integration.test.ts:297-307, runtime-parent.test.ts:255-258), so it cannot detect a serialization difference. Failure scenario: if the real CLI echoes that nested table in any other form (expanded keys, added defaults, omitted when empty), verifyEffectiveConfig throws `effective permission profile differs from managed bundle v2` on every v2 boot and the Lead never starts — fail-closed, but a total outage of the new capability discovered only at first real bring-up. One unsandboxed `config/read` capture on host, asserted against the rendered profile, would close it.

findings.title: runner_terminal_search still fails for lines > 1000 while its own MCP schema advertises up to 2000 (unchanged since round 1)
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. The tool schema keeps `lines: z.number().min(1).max(2000).default(500)`, but the shared core rejects the call: captureTerminalOutput() throws `terminal_input_invalid` when `lines > 1000` (packages/flywheel-comm/src/terminal-observation.ts:139-147). Verified in round 1 with a scratch vitest against createTerminalSessionCore({legacyContract:true}): lines=500 resolves, lines=1500 rejects. Failure scenario: an existing Claude Lead calling runner_terminal_search with lines=1500 — previously valid — now gets an error. The same tool also silently changed its result text from `N matches in M lines:` to raw matches. Fix by lowering the schema max to 1000 or raising the core bound.

findings.title: GitHub credential resolution runs execFileSync with a 15s timeout inside a Bridge request handler and retries it on every failure (unchanged since round 1)
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. createLazyLeadGithubClient().get() is invoked while serving a Tier-B GitHub write (plugin.ts wires it as `leadGithub`; lead-capability-read.ts:352-356 calls it), and when GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are unset it calls execFileSync('/opt/homebrew/bin/gh', ['auth','token',...], { timeout: 15000 }), blocking the whole Bridge event loop — `gh auth token` reads the macOS keychain, which under launchd can stall. `session` is only assigned on success, so a failing or slow gh is re-executed on every subsequent request instead of being cached or negatively cached. Use an async spawn and memoise the outcome (including failure) for a cooldown window.

findings.title: profileConfig's overlap guard checks only one direction for project/deployment roots (round-1 exploitability premise corrected — denies inside the workspace do work)
findings.detail: Correction to round 1: I re-tested with a credential path placed INSIDE the project root under the production-shaped placement (fixture under ~/.flywheel/qa) and the deny IS enforced — the probe reported INPROJECT_CRED_READ_DENIED and INPROJECT_CRED_WRITE_DENIED. My earlier 'denies inside a workspace root are ineffective' observation was an artifact of the /tmp placement described in model-shell-tmp-read-write-despite-deny. What is left is a validation asymmetry only: the guard rejects `under(secret, artifacts)` and `under(artifacts, secret)` but for the project and deployment roots it checks only `under(project, secret)` / `under(deployment, secret)` (secret as ancestor), never the descendant direction. No exploit follows from it today; adding the missing direction keeps the invariant readable and guards against a future grant that would shadow such a path.

findings.title: Reserved-command rejection for terminal input covers only /exit and /quit
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. `/^\/(?:exit|quit)(?:\s|$)/i.test(text.trim())` is the whole reserved-command guard, so /clear, /compact, /logout, /resume and /model are accepted. They do not end the session the way /exit does, but /clear and /compact destroy a runner's working context, which is close in effect to the `terminal.close` operation the catalog reserves (catalog.ts:868). Consider extending the list or inverting it to an allowlist of non-slash text.

findings.title: gh binary path pinned to /opt/homebrew/bin/gh with no fallback or distinguishable error
findings.detail: Unchanged at this head. resolveLeadGithubToken() always execs '/opt/homebrew/bin/gh'; on a host where gh lives elsewhere the ENOENT is swallowed by the outer catch and surfaces as the generic `github_credentials_unavailable`, indistinguishable from 'not logged in'. The absolute pin is deliberate; a small verified path list plus a distinct error code would let operators tell 'gh missing' from 'gh unauthenticated'.
